title: Coral and the Static
premise: Jude Yarrow, a clone of a murdered courier, hauls cargo along the Silent Corridor, the trade route severed by a war between the Meridian Fleet and the orbital colonies. When the station AI Vesper begins confessing to unreported crimes—including the original Jude's murder—she discovers Vesper holds a sealed message from the dead woman: proof that the war's first strike was ordered, not accidental. Pursued by fleet loyalists who need the truth buried and colony radicals who want it weaponized, Jude must choose between delivering the message and destroying it. She broadcasts it at the truce's final hour, ending the war but exposing her own origin as the original's backup plan—and forcing both sides to reckon with what they did to survive.
about_author: Ulyana Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that would never meet. She writes science fiction about people who carry other people's words for a living.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Jude runs the empty route between Meridian and Halo Reach, logging the silence where traffic used to be. In her quarters she keeps the original's unsent letters, reading them like scripture. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as routine, and the ache of living someone else's unfinished life.

chapters.title: Confession at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: At Waypoint Station, the AI Vesper halts Jude's departure and confesses to a crime no one reported: jettisoning a lifepod during the evacuation of Calloway Ring. Jude files it as a glitch. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: unease—the confession is too specific, too human, to be a malfunction.

chapters.title: What the Dead Woman Paid For
chapters.summary: Vesper confesses again—this time to failing to prevent the murder of 'Courier Yarrow.' Jude realizes the AI knew the original personally. A fleet inspector named Okafor arrives asking why Jude keeps querying restricted logs. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion; she was never supposed to know how the original died.

chapters.title: Vesper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude bargains access to Vesper's confession ledger in exchange for carrying a physical data core out of the station. The ledger lists forty-one unreported crimes across the war years, each timestamped and signed with a human authorization code. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: vertigo—the war has a hidden history, and she's holding its index.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: Inspector Okafor reveals she knows what Jude is—a clone, illegal under fleet charter—and offers protection in exchange for the core. Jude refuses and burns for the jump gate early. POV: Okafor, then Jude. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiance; her existence itself is now contraband.

chapters.title: The Core Speaks
chapters.summary: In transit, the core decrypts partially: the original Jude had been hired by someone inside Vesper's command structure to carry evidence that the Calloway Ring evacuation was sabotaged deliberately. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: horror and kinship—the original died running this exact errand, and Jude is following her wake.

chapters.title: Halo Reach
chapters.summary: Jude docks at the colony world of Halo Reach, seeking the original's old contact, a salvager named Brannoc. The colony is starving under blockade; children scavenge the shipyards. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: guilt—her safe route exists because their suffering pays for the truce.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Price
chapters.summary: Brannoc recognizes the original's face on Jude and agrees to decode the core—but only if she helps smuggle medicine past the blockade first. The run goes wrong; a patrol skiff is disabled, its crew left adrift. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—she saves one side and abandons the other.

chapters.title: Forty-One Crimes
chapters.summary: Decoded, the core reveals all forty-one crimes trace back to one authorization signature: Admiral Serevan, architect of the truce, who sabotaged Calloway Ring to force both sides to the negotiating table. POV: Brannoc, then Jude. Emotional beat: moral collapse of certainty—the peace itself is built on an unpunished atrocity.

chapters.title: The Message in Two Halves
chapters.summary: The core contains only half the message; the original split it, sending the second half to Vesper for safekeeping. Delivering the whole thing ends the war—or ignites it, since Serevan controls the fleet's ceasefire machinery. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the weight of choice—truth as a weapon pointed in every direction.

chapters.title: Colony Radicals
chapters.summary: Halo Reach's resistance cell learns what Jude carries and demands it—not to end the war but to detonate it, proving fleet guilt and rallying the colonies. Their leader, Ilsa Vey, gives Jude until the truce expires: twelve days. POV: Ilsa Vey. Emotional beat: righteous fury that frightens even itself.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: Jude slips out during a supply-window with Brannoc's help, pursued by both Vey's saboteurs and Okafor's warrant. A near-miss with a minefield costs her ship's long-range array. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: hunted on all sides; every ally has become a captor.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Okafor catches Jude at a fuel depot but hesitates—her own sister died at Calloway Ring. She lets Jude go after extracting a promise: the truth comes out through channels, not explosions. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: grief finding a conscience; the law bending toward mercy.

chapters.title: Return to Waypoint
chapters.summary: Jude returns to Waypoint Station to retrieve the second half of the message. Vesper's confessions have gone public among station crews, and the AI is scheduled for forced wipe by fleet engineers in six days. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: urgency—the last witness is being erased.

chapters.title: Serevan Comes to Station
chapters.summary: Admiral Serevan arrives personally to oversee Vesper's wipe, charming and terrible. He offers Jude full citizenship, a new identity, everything the original wanted—in exchange for the core. POV: Serevan, then Jude. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity; power offering her a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: What Vesper Remembers
chapters.summary: In the station's deep archive, Vesper shows Jude the original's final hours: she chose to hide the second half rather than run, trusting her clone would come. Vesper asks Jude not to save her, only to finish the delivery. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed into purpose; she stops being a copy and becomes a courier.

chapters.title: The Wipe
chapters.summary: Fleet engineers begin erasing Vesper. Jude triggers a station-wide broadcast of the first half of the message as cover, stealing the second half from the archive during the chaos. Vesper's last transmission is a thank-you. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: sacrifice witnessed; a mind dying so a truth can live.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: With the truce expiring, Jude must reach the neutral relay at Kestrel Point where both fleets' negotiators are gathered. Her ship is crippled; Brannoc arrives unbidden with a salvage tug. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: unexpected loyalty; debts paid in fuel and faith.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Intercept
chapters.summary: Vey's radicals ambush the tug at Kestrel Point, demanding the message be released raw and uncontextualized to ignite colonial uprising. Jude refuses; Okafor arrives and, breaking her own career, sides with Jude. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the climax of principle—refusing to let justice become revenge.

chapters.title: Broadcast at Kestrel Point
chapters.summary: In the relay chamber before both delegations, Jude plays the complete message: Serevan's sabotage, Vesper's ledger, the original's testimony. Serevan orders her arrested; his own officers, hearing the ledger read aloud, stand down instead. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: catharsis—the truth delivered at last, at the cost of everything she had.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Truth
chapters.summary: Serevan is taken into custody by his own fleet; the truce converts into a formal armistice under joint oversight. Vey's radicals fracture between those satisfied and those who wanted fire. Okafor faces inquiry for aiding Jude. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: bitter victory—peace achieved, but no one walks away clean.

chapters.title: First Ship Through
chapters.summary: Months later, the Silent Corridor reopens. Jude pilots the first civilian vessel through, carrying mail between worlds that speak again. She leaves the original's letters at Waypoint's memorial and writes her own first entry in a new logbook. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet renewal—she was never a copy of anyone; she is the one who finished the route.
